title: The speech the bride wrote for me
author: Storytime
hook: The bride wrote my maid of honor speech herself. Halfway through reading it, I realized what it was really about.
story: My best friend Lauren got married last Saturday. A month before, she handed me an envelope and said, this is your speech. I wrote it for you. Please read it exactly as it is. Don't change a single word. I thought that was strange, but she's a control freak, so okay. At the reception, I stood up and started reading. It began sweet. How she met Mark. Their first trip. Then it got oddly specific. I read, Mark, thank you for every Tuesday you said you were at the gym. Thank you for the hotel in Denver in March. And thank you, Jessica, for being such a good friend to both of us. Jessica was a bridesmaid. Sitting at the head table. The room went completely silent. I looked at Lauren. She was smiling. Calm. She had found out two weeks before the wedding. She didn't cancel, because his parents paid for everything and refused a refund. So she let the wedding happen, and let me read the truth in front of everyone. Mark stood up and grabbed the microphone from my hand. And then Lauren stood up too, and said, let her finish, there's one more page. Part two?
caption: she told me not to change a single word 🥂 #storytime
sound: a slow, elegant string quartet with rising tension at very low volume
why: Bridesmaid and wedding drama is a constant top storytime genre, the order not to change a word is the planted clue, and the one more page line is a strong part two hook.

title: Coworker dressed as me for Halloween
author: Storytime
hook: My coworker won the office Halloween contest dressed as me. Then the CEO walked in.
story: Our office does a Halloween costume contest every year. The prize is a day off. This year my coworker Tyler showed up dressed as me. Same glasses. Same blue lanyard. My giant coffee mug. He even had a stack of sticky notes on his chest, because I'm famous for leaving notes on everyone's desk. Honestly, it was hilarious. He won by a landslide. Then the CEO walked in. She'd been at our headquarters all year, and she'd never met most of us in person. She walked straight up to Tyler, shook his hand, and said, you must be Marcus. Your project saved us half a million dollars this year. I wanted to meet you before the promotion announcement. Marcus is me. Tyler froze. Everyone looked at me. And Tyler, still holding my coffee mug, said, thank you, it was a team effort. He didn't correct her. The CEO left for the airport an hour later. And this morning, the promotion announcement went out to the whole company. With Tyler's name on it. My manager says she'll sort it out. Tyler says it was just a joke that got out of hand. So should I email the CEO myself, or let my manager handle it?
caption: he took my look AND my promotion 🎃 #storytime
sound: a quirky, mischievous Halloween beat at very low volume
why: Posted on Halloween with a fun visual setup, the costume details make the mix-up believable, and the final question splits commenters between going straight to the CEO or trusting the manager.

title: Grandma's secret recipe contest
author: Storytime
hook: My aunt entered my late grandma's secret cake recipe in a contest as her own. Grandma saw it coming.
story: My grandma made the best caramel apple cake in our town. Everyone begged for the recipe. She always said, never trust a recipe card you didn't watch me make. When she passed last year, my aunt Linda took the recipe box. This fall, Linda entered a baking contest on our local TV station. Her cake was called Linda's famous caramel apple cake. The judges took one bite. One of them actually coughed. Another said, is there salt in the caramel? Linda had used the recipe card from the box. Word for word. What she didn't know is that Grandma wrote a fake card years ago. Two tablespoons of salt instead of sugar. On purpose. The real recipe was in a sealed envelope, with my name on it. Grandma taught me to make that cake every Sunday when I was a kid. She told me, one day someone will try to take this. Let them. Now Linda says I sabotaged her. And the TV station wants the real cake for their holiday special. Should I do it?
caption: never trust a recipe card you didn't watch her make 🍎 #storytime
sound: a warm, cozy fall acoustic guitar at very low volume
why: Holiday baking season plus a karma twist, grandma's line about recipe cards is the planted clue, and the TV special question lets viewers cheer for the narrator in the comments.
